selection: Confirmed or controversial planets with a catalog duration and a mid-time uncertainty of at most 30 minutes at the start; windows that are "full" (dark, Sun below -12 degrees, star above 30 degrees throughout the padded window); per site and night the deepest first, then earliest, at most 40.
windowRule: A window is the transit from ingress to egress padded on each side by a fixed baseline plus k times the 1-sigma mid-time uncertainty (sigma = sqrt(sigma_T0^2 + (n sigma_P)^2)). It is "full" when every sample of the padded window (every 2 minutes) is in the dark (Sun below the twilight limit) with the star above the altitude limit, below the airmass limit and within the hour-angle limit when those are set; "transit only" when the transit itself is but the padding is not; "partial" otherwise, with the share of the transit that is. Secondary eclipses and quadratures are circular-orbit estimates at phases 0.5, 0.25 and 0.75 (no eccentricity is applied).
ephemerisSource: transit-ephemerides.json.gz (one catalog row per planet; see its selectionPolicy)
claimBoundary: Geometric predictions from catalog ephemerides with almanac-accuracy Sun and Moon; no weather, refraction, horizon or telescope limits. Check the ephemeris before observing.
